threads.body: [minor] add some javadoc to explain it makes the matching conditional on the predicate.

I don't think capturing those attributes provide relevant information in the context of metrics:
- `camel.version` relates to the version of the library used in the application, so it's more about implementation dependencies than something that will change over time. However knowing which version of camel is used is something meaningful to know, but metric attribute is probably not the best way to capture and send this information, it would be more relevant as a resource attribute for example (and we probably have other ways to capture this information).
- `camel.class_resolver` : I don't know about the actual value of this attribute, but this seems to be more an implementation detail that contains a technical information like a class name or a high-cardinality value if it's a `toString` of an object that changes on every JVM execution. From the metrics perspective, does it help to provide a relevant breakdown on the metrics ? If no I would suggest to drop it.

Also, none of them will change at runtime over the execution of the JVM.

Because those are MBean attributes, removing them would not cause extra aggregation as we had with Jetty where an MBean "technical" parameter `id=*` is ignored (and thus we aggregate in the rare case where there is more than one value).

threads.body:
For those three metrics, I think it would be better to replace them with

- `camel.threadpool.thread.min`: replaces `camel.threadpool.pool.core.size`, it is effectively the minimum number of threads in the pool, even if they are idle (the difference is that it's a "configured minimum" rather than an "observed minimum").
- `camel.threadpool.thread.count`: replaces `camel.threadpool.pool.size.current`
- `camel.threadpool.thread.limit`: capture the configured upper limit for `thread.count` (`MaximumPoolSize` attribute)

I think that we discard capturing the `.max` as we capture the current value and the backend will do a better job to provide it. The reason we still capture the `.min` here is that the backend won´t be able to know which value is configured as minimum pool size (which this metric provides).

I know that the `threadpool.thread.*` might seem a bit redundant, but we also have `threadpool.task.*` below, so I think this is fine.

The descriptions of thread related metrics state:
- `camel.threadpool.pool.core.size`: The number of threads that are always kept in the pool, even if they are idle.
- `camel.threadpool.pool.size.current`: The current number of threads in the pool.
- `camel.threadpool.pool.size.max`: The largest number of threads that have ever simultaneously been in the pool.

So `camel.threadpool.pool.size.max` should not be renamed to `camel.threadpool.thread.limit` I think.
I'd rename `camel.threadpool.pool.size.current` and `camel.threadpool.pool.size.max` to `camel.threadpool.thread.count` and `camel.threadpool.thread.max` respectively.

`camel.threadpool.pool.core.size` could be renamed to `camel.threadpool.thread.limit.lower` (this would let us add `camel.threadpool.thread.limit.upper` if needed)

Using `lower` and `upper` for the limit is a good idea here, I think we should have both `camel.threadpool.thread.limit.upper` and `camel.threadpool.thread.limit.lower` to make the intent behind this choice clear. This also removes the ambiguity to have a `.min` that is in fact not a pre-aggregation from the observation of a metric but something we can act on through camel configuration.

This means adding `camel.threadpool.thread.limit.upper` metric from the `MaximumPoolSize` MBean attribute which was not previously captured.

For the `camel.threadpool.thread.max` (`LargestPoolSize` MBean attribute), this is just a pre-aggregation of the `camel.threadpool.thread.count` (`PoolSize` MBean attribute), so this is something that would be better provided by the backend.
This would be something that goes against recommendations added in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/16212

> For the `camel.threadpool.thread.max` (LargestPoolSize MBean attribute), this is just a pre-aggregation of the `camel.threadpool.thread.count`

In some cases it may not be correct assumption. Backend will know only about state of the threadpool at the times of metric scraping. Sometimes it may be a peak in number of threads that happens between scraping points and backend will not know this basing on `camel.threadpool.thread.count`, but will know basing on `camel.threadpool.thread.max`

I agree, we have no guarantee that an intermediate value between two samples could be missed, however I think this should be a corner case, unless the sampling frequency is very low.

We can leave it if you think that's useful, also it was already present before so at least it provides an equivalent metric for migration if needed.
